findings.title: Mobile modal light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30%
findings.description: The `.custom-message-length` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value is now 30% instead of 70%, so the text will render much darker on light backgrounds. Every other conversion in this diff keeps the original primary lightness. The desktop equivalent in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly keeps 70%.

findings.title: Desktop user name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.description: The `.name` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. The primary value is silently changed from 30% to 50%, so user names render lighter than before. The same slip appears in the `.name` rule at `desktop/user.scss:522` and the matching block in `mobile/user.scss:497`.

findings.title: Mobile user name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.description: The `.name` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The primary lightness is changed from 30% to 50%, which is not part of a dark/light conversion and alters the light theme.

findings.title: Mobile topic-post heading light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.description: The `h3` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The primary value is changed from 20% to 50%, making the heading noticeably lighter. The secondary value (50%) also does not match the 80% secondary used for the equivalent desktop heading.

findings.title: Desktop post author link light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70%
findings.description: The `a` color inside the post-author block changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The primary value jumps from 30% to 70%, which will render the link almost invisible on light backgrounds. The secondary value (30%) appears to be copied from the 70% rule rather than the original 30% rule.
